passage: Saurabh, I saw your fists when the officer at the ward office barked at your father last week. I know that feeling. When I was ten, a clerk shouted at my father over a stamp on some papers, and I wanted to shout back and run away in the same breath. My chest was hot and my legs felt useless. My father folded the papers, said calmly, "We'll go to the proper counter," and we left. Next week he went again with his brother, and it got done. I'm Chetan, your Dada, and I'm telling you this because loud voices don't mean the loud person is right. Your parents are sorting it out. You just tell me when it burns.

qa.q: Who barked at Saurabh's father at the ward office?
qa.a: The officer at the ward office barked at him.

qa.q: What do Saurabh's fists suggest about Saurabh's feelings?
qa.a: Anger and helplessness at seeing Saurabh's father spoken to unfairly.

qa.q: What is a safe way for Saurabh to handle the anger?
qa.a: Saurabh can leave the matter to the parents and talk about how it burns with Dada, instead of confronting the officer directly.

qa.q: How might Saurabh's father have felt when the clerk shouted in Chetan's story?
qa.a: Probably hurt and humiliated, yet he stayed calm, left, and went back through the proper counter with his brother.

grounding: Shows an elder recalling when an official was rude to his family, the anger and powerlessness, and calm handling by a parent.

passage:
Monday: At the ration office, Karthik and Appa waited in line for two hours. When they reached the window, the clerk didn't look up. "Wrong form. Come next week." When Appa politely asked which form, the clerk snapped, "Can't you read?" and waved them away. Karthik's hands balled into fists. He wanted to shout that Appa reads Tamil and English. But the clerk had the stamp, and they had nothing.
Tuesday: Karthik told his friend Pankaj. "He was rude just because he could be," Karthik said, still hot. Pankaj nodded. "My mother says a stamp doesn't make someone right."
The next Monday: Appa went back with the correct form and a written complaint for the senior officer. Karthik watched him stay calm. The senior officer apologised and stamped the card in five minutes.

qa.q: How long did Karthik and Appa wait in line?
How did Karthik feel when the clerk snapped at Appa?
qa.a: Angry and powerless; his hands balled into fists, but the clerk had the stamp.

qa.q: How did Appa handle the unfairness safely?
qa.a: He stayed calm, came back with the correct form and gave a written complaint to the senior officer.

qa.q: What did Pankaj's mother's saying mean?
qa.a: That having power, like a stamp, does not make someone right.

grounding: A boy angry and powerless at an official's rudeness to his father sees his father handle it calmly and properly.

passage: Gopika, you're still angry at the guard who shouted at your Amma at the hospital gate? Come, your Charu Ammamma understands. When I was your age, the land clerk came to our village to measure fields. He called my father an "illiterate fool" in front of everyone, because Appa asked him to measure again. My face burned. I wanted to throw a stone at his big umbrella. I felt so small and helpless. But Appa only folded his hands and said, "Sir, I will come to the taluk office." The next week he went with the village elders and a written paper. The officer there made the clerk measure again, and Appa got his correct land. A big post doesn't make someone right, Gopika. And your Amma will handle that guard the proper way, with the hospital manager.

qa.q: What did the land clerk call young Charu's father?
How did young Charu feel when the clerk insulted her father?
qa.a: Angry, small and helpless; her face burned and she wanted to throw a stone.

qa.q: What choice in Ammamma's story fixed the unfairness?
qa.a: Appa stayed calm and went to the taluk office with the village elders and a written paper.

qa.q: How might Appa have felt when he was insulted?
qa.a: Hurt and humiliated, but he chose to stay calm and use the proper way.

grounding: A grandmother recalls feeling angry and powerless when an official insulted her father, and how he handled it safely through proper channels.
